clue.text: In America, doing these crosswords, ultimately grows old

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each word in the run before it

explanation.surface: Somewhere in the States, working through these puzzles gradually makes a person older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last letters of America, doing, these and crosswords; 'In' is only a link, its N not used.
explanation.definitionFit: To age is to become older, a plain verb synonym of the phrase.

clue.text: Foreign girl's name from strange language

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A girl from abroad has a name drawn from some odd tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' finds the run straddling strANGE LAnguage. The name was topical as that of the German chancellor, and Lady Angela is a character in the G&S operetta Patience.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela is a feminine given name, borne by a famous German head of government.

clue.text: End of rally in game with Irish county, say

parts.note: monte is a gambling card game

indicators.note: say signals that the county's name is used for its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: Carlow is a county in the south-east of Ireland

explanation.surface: Finishing a car rally while playing cards somewhere in rural Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous Monte Carlo Rally traditionally finishes in Monaco's resort town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Monaco resort is the traditional finishing point of the famous motor rally named after it.

clue.text: Canned music, note — result of fitting punishment for cheat?

definitions.text: result of fitting punishment for cheat?

indicators.note: canned is slang for drunk, so the letters of the word beside it are in disorder

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Recorded music plus a note, followed by an aside about a cheat getting what he deserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canned' looks like 'pre-recorded' but means drunk, scrambling MUSIC. In The Mikado the billiard sharp's punishment is to play with a twisted cue, so a botched shot results.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscue is a faulty stroke in billiards, the natural outcome of being forced to use a bent cue.

clue.text: Royal person in front of crowd, surrounded by journalists

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the following pieces inside the journalists

parts.note: the press is the body of journalists

indicators.note: front of takes the first letter of the word crowd

explanation.surface: A royal stands before the crowd, hemmed in by reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal person' looks like the subject of the surface but is the definition. Princess Ida is a G&S operetta.
explanation.definitionFit: A princess is a female member of a royal family, so a royal person.

clue.text: Informally, reformed character and king dined together

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
ate is the past tense of eat, to dine

explanation.surface: A reformed person and a monarch shared a meal, put casually.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate is the familiar form of Katherine, the shrew tamed and reformed in Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's shrew Katherine is called Kate by Petruchio and ends the play transformed in temper.

clue.text: Protective garment used by chap in a forest

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some protective clothing worn by a man out in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles chaP IN A FOREst; HMS Pinafore is a G&S operetta.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is an apron-like overgarment worn to keep clothes clean.

clue.text: In hearing, why are you rising after judge and accused's 20?

indicators.note: after places the turned letters behind the judge's letter
in a down entry rising means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
In hearing says the words are taken by their sound, as letters

parts.note: spoken, the three words sound like the letters Y, R and U

explanation.surface: A question asked aloud in a courtroom about why someone stands up after the judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is PEERS: a defendant is tried by a jury of their peers. Trial by Jury is a G&S operetta.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury is traditionally made up of the defendant's equals, ordinary citizens judging one of their own.

clue.text: Propeller of boat, liner good at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of the preceding words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Something that drives a vessel: a good liner out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges LINERGOOD; The Gondoliers is a G&S operetta.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondolier pushes a Venetian gondola along with a single oar.

clue.text: 5 backed by multinational group for so long

parts.note: 5-down is PRINCESS; a princess is A DI, after the late Princess Diana
EU is the European Union

explanation.surface: A royal supported by a European bloc, heading off for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed by' is a link here, putting EU behind A DI.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are ways of saying goodbye, the French one used in English for a farewell.

clue.text: Adorable royal I spotted in dramatic location

indicators.note: spotted in says the royal pronoun was seen inside the location

parts.note: a set is the scenery where a play or film is staged
the royal we is how a monarch says I

explanation.surface: A cute royal appearance on a stage or film set.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal we is the monarch's way of saying I, so 'royal I' means the pronoun a sovereign uses for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet and adorable both describe something charming and lovable.

clue.text: Rebuilt entrance ahead of year that's special anniversary

indicators.note: ahead of puts the rebuilt word in front of the year's letter
rebuilt says the letters of entrance are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A reconstructed doorway is ready in time for a big commemoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebuilt' turns ENTRANCE into CENTENAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A centenary marks a hundred years, a notable milestone among anniversaries.

clue.text: Name of female Australian film star (6, say), missing last two parts

indicators.note: missing last two parts drops the final pair of letters from the surname

parts.note: Cate Blanchett is an Australian actor whose first name sounds like 6-down's answer

explanation.surface: Naming an Aussie actress, but leaving off the end of her name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing last two parts' cuts TT from BLANCHETT. Lady Blanche is a character in Princess Ida.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanche is a feminine given name, from the French for white.

clue.text: American money for one of the county set

definitions.meaning: dollars are informally called ... in the US
The usual short name of Buckinghamshire, one of the English counties

explanation.walkthrough: 'county set' suggests the landed gentry, but it is the set of English counties. Buckinghamshire is a county just north-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Dollars are bucks in American slang, and Bucks is a standard abbreviated name of Buckinghamshire.

clue.text: The very model of it, found in English fruit

indicators.note: found in puts the word it inside the fruit

parts.note: a pome is a fruit such as an apple or pear

explanation.surface: Echoing the Major-General's song: perfection discovered inside an apple from England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am the very model of a modern Major-General' is from The Pirates of Penzance.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect example, the ideal instance of a type.

clue.text: Results of fouling? Umpire is mad about it

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go round the word it
mad says the letters of the words beside it run wild

explanation.surface: A referee furious over fouls on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' scrambles the umpire letters. 'fouling' suggests football, but it means making dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: Fouling something makes it dirty, leaving contaminants in it.

clue.text: Winds up ditching Conservative as leader for moderates

indicators.note: ditching says the party's letter is thrown out from the word

parts.note: to wind up is to end, as ceases does

explanation.surface: A politician wraps things up by dumping the Tory leader to placate the centrists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as leader' tells you the C comes off the front of CEASES.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to lessen or soften, so moderates in the verb sense.

clue.text: Dealer, one with unhappy lot, half-hearted?

indicators.note: half-hearted removes half of the doubled letter at the word's centre

parts.note: in The Pirates of Penzance a policeman's lot is not a happy one, and a policeman is a copper

explanation.surface: A trader who puts up with a poor deal, without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one of the two Ps in COPPER, the heart of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A coper is an old word for a dealer, especially in horses.

clue.text: Game one plays that's said to be virtuous

definitions.meaning: a card game played alone, called solitaire in America
a proverb holds that this quality is a virtue

explanation.walkthrough: Patience is also a G&S operetta.
explanation.definitionFit: The solo card game and the calm quality share a name, the latter proverbially a virtue.

clue.text: Today's theme, initially — source of amusement

definitions.meaning: the puzzle's theme is Gilbert and Sullivan, and its first letters are G, A and S
something hilarious is informally called this in British slang

explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of Gilbert And Sullivan; 'it was a gas' is British slang for great fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is a gas is great fun, an informal synonym.

clue.text: What's odd on flag and on old banner

indicators.note: odd says the letters of the following words are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Asking what is strange about this flag and that old banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges ONFLAG; 'and' is only a link before the second on.
explanation.definitionFit: A gonfalon is a medieval standard hung from a crossbar, as used by Italian city-states.

clue.text: Looks for some people in the other place

definitions.text: some people in the other place
definitions.meaning: the other place is what the House of Commons calls the House of Lords, whose members are lords

explanation.walkthrough: The chorus of Iolanthe is made up of members of the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to look intently, and members of the House of Lords are peers.

clue.text: Protest something you can't stand for

definitions.meaning: a demonstration where people occupy a place sitting
a meal or event where everyone is seated, so no standing

explanation.definitionFit: A sit-down is both a seated demonstration and a seated meal, where nobody stands.

clue.text: Destroyers at sea changing sides in course of exercises

indicators.note: changing sides swaps left for right, L for R

parts.note: Pilates is a system of exercises for core strength

explanation.surface: Warships at sea, switching allegiance during a fitness class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroyers' looks naval, but it means plunderers. The Pirates of Penzance is a G&S operetta.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirates attack and destroy ships on the open sea.

clue.text: Suitable publicity covering most of 18, for example

indicators.note: covering puts the publicity on top in this down entry

parts.note: PR is public relations, publicity

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter

parts.note: 18-down, Patience, is an example of an opera

explanation.surface: Fitting promotion for most of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: OPERA loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper and suitable both mean appropriate or fitting.

clue.text: Hit disastrously with freak try — a score and a half

indicators.note: disastrously says the letters of hit go badly wrong
freak says the letters of try are oddly arranged

explanation.surface: A rugby player strikes badly, then scores a fluke try.
explanation.walkthrough: HIT becomes THI and TRY becomes RTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so one and a half scores make thirty.

clue.text: Emperor and unruly kid at home

indicators.note: unruly says the letters of the following words are out of order

explanation.surface: A monarch and a badly behaved child at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges KIDATHOME; The Mikado is a G&S operetta.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikado is an old title for the emperor of Japan.

clue.text: It's needed by diplomat, actually

indicators.note: needed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diplomat really does need it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' cannot define the answer alone; the whole clue is the definition, and the wordplay is the run across diplomaT ACTually.
explanation.definitionFit: Tact, delicacy in handling people, is the quality a diplomat must have.

clue.text: Composer deleting first half ruler described as terrible

indicators.note: deleting first half removes the opening half of the composer's name

parts.note: Arthur Sullivan composed the music for the G&S operettas

explanation.surface: A composer cuts his opening section about a fearsome monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: SULLIVAN loses SULL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan IV of Russia is known to history as Ivan the Terrible.

clue.text: Ordeal that's terminable, oddly enough

indicators.note: oddly enough selects the odd-numbered letters of the word before it

explanation.surface: A hardship which, strangely, can be brought to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th letters of terminable; Trial by Jury is a G&S operetta.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a painful test of endurance, as an ordeal is.

clue.text: Desire or inclination — that of 28, we hear, was little

definitions.meaning: ... is an old word for desire, and a ship's ... is its lean or inclination

definitions.text: that of 28, we hear, was little
definitions.meaning: 28 is COCOA, which sounds like Ko-Ko

explanation.definitionFit: List is an archaic word for wish and also a sideways lean; Ko-Ko's list in The Mikado is famously little.

clue.text: Hot drink found in eg Yorkshire/Lancashire area

parts.note: Yorkshire is an example of a county, abbreviated CO
Lancashire is another county, CO again

explanation.surface: A warm drink found across the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire and Lancashire are neighbouring counties in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate drink made from powdered cacao.

clue.text: Less serious works of kind poet rates poorly

indicators.note: poorly says the letters of the preceding words are badly arranged

explanation.surface: Lighter pieces of a sort that a poet holds in low regard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' rearranges POETRATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Operettas are light operas, less weighty than grand opera, as the G&S works are.
